LESSON: SELF-CONTROL

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Church
Topic 5.6: Self-control

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Self-control. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you practice self- control?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELF-CONTROL
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Self-control helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SELF-CONTROL
Study Self-control like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Self-control” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Self-control is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Self-control” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Self-control to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Self-control from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Self-control: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Self-control?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you practice self- control?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Self-control means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
